subject: Food Science
title: Aroma and Memory
description: A quick, practical guide to Aroma and Memory.

hook.text: The smell of cinnamon might teleport you to your grandmother's kitchen. Smell triggers memory more powerfully than any other.

buildup.text: The olfactory bulb connects directly to the amygdala (emotion) and hippocampus (memory).

discovery.text: The 'Proust effect' describes smell-triggered memories that feel vivid and emotional.

twist.text: Odor preferences are mostly learned, not innate. Vanilla smells 'good' to Westerners but can seem medicinal in cultures where.

climax.text: Companies use scent marketing deliberately. Real-estate agents bake cookies during open houses.

punchline.text: Smell bypasses thought and hits emotion first. That's why a single whiff can unlock.

quiz.question: Why does smell trigger memories so powerfully?
options: Smells are louder than other stimuli
The olfactory bulb connects directly to the amygdala and hippocampus
Smell has more receptors than sight
